edges.description: SLC6A1 loss-of-function variants impair the GAT-1 GABA transporter.
Impaired GABA transport dysregulates phasic and tonic inhibitory signaling.
Thalamocortical hypersynchrony produces generalized spike-wave discharges.
Generalized discharges produce the clinical seizures.
The seizure endpoint is observed clinically as the hallmark myoclonic-atonic seizure.
Loss of postural tone in the seizure produces the atonic drop attack.
Myoclonic jerks without a following atonic component also occur.
The generalized discharge also manifests as absence seizures.
Generalized tonic-clonic seizures are part of the seizure repertoire.
A substantial minority develop intellectual disability; whether this follows from seizure burden, the underlying genetic lesion, or both is not resolved, so the intermediates are left unspecified.

nodes.description: EMAtS has a strong but genetically heterogeneous basis. The best-established single gene is SLC6A1 (GABA transporter GAT-1); other contributors overlap the GEFS+ spectrum (SCN1A, SCN1B, GABRG2), and the overall architecture is usually complex/polygenic. This node captures the single concept of the predisposing genetic variation.

nodes.description: Loss-of-function SLC6A1 variants impair GAT-1, the presynaptic/astrocytic GABA transporter that clears GABA from the synapse and shapes inhibitory signaling. This node captures the single concept of the transporter defect and conforms to the shared epilepsy final common pathway.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in the GABA Transporter SLC6A1 Cause Epilepsy with Myoclonic-Atonic Seizures.
evidence.snippet: GAT-1, encoded by SLC6A1, is one of the major gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA) transporters in the brain and is responsible for re-uptake of GABA from the synapse. ... In this study, targeted resequencing of 644 individuals with epileptic encephalopathies led to the identification of six SLC6A1 mutations in seven individuals, all of whom have epilepsy with myoclonic-atonic seizures (MAE). ... Overall, pathogenic mutations occurred in 6/160 individuals with MAE, accounting for ~4% of unsolved MAE cases.
